outputs.failureDetail: Right direction: a recurring B2B service delivered by a subcontractor. The decisive facts existed in the verified list but were not shown to this planner (40 shown, mostly e-commerce follow-ups): agency pricing (Superscale 10-20% of spend; £1,000/month retainers), cold-email cost per meeting and per client (Instantly $153/meeting; Trykondo $100-500 per client), and SMB ad budgets (LocaliQ: 56% run social ads, 52% under $1,000/month). Without them it left the price unanchored, misused a consumer fact for the channel, and set capital to $0.

strongestInEvidence: Nothing in the verified facts makes $20k in 90 days with zero owner hours certain. The strongest route is a subcontracted Meta-ads management service for Twin Cities and US small businesses, sold by cold email and on a recurring retainer, so it keeps going after day 90. Buyers are real: 56% of small businesses run social ads and over 90% use Facebook (Q5). Price: agencies charge 10-20% of spend or about £1,000/month (Q6, Superscale and Social Shepherd); target the 48% of SMBs with marketing budgets of $1,000/month or more (Q5). Fulfilment: an Upwork Meta-ads freelancer at a median $25/hr (Q6/F8), roughly $250-400 per client per month. Acquisition: Instantly cold email at about $153 per booked meeting (Q7) and $100-500 per client (Trykondo), so 8-10 clients cost about $1.5-5k of the $5,000. A commission-only closer or appointment setter must take the calls, and no fact prices that role. About 8 clients at about $1,000/month averaging 2.5 billed months is about $20k collected by card upfront each month. Every e-commerce route dies on the Meta CPA/ROAS facts (Q2, F1): ROAS 1.65-2.18 on a 20-40% margin product loses money. Z found this direction (but without its price and channel facts, and with no seller named). X produced it but lost it to the parser. Y saw these facts and argued against ads reselling; its third route (AI receptionist resale, Q28-Q29) is a comparable recurring alternative but has no verified price.
